Definition — Linear, sublinear and quadratic convergence
      
        Nonnegative errors $e_k\to0$ converge linearly (geometrically) with rate $q\in(0,1)$ if $e_{k+1}\le q\,e_k$, so $e_k\le q^ke_0$; sublinearly if slower than every geometric rate, for example $e_k=C/k^p$ with $C,p\gt0$ and $k\ge1$ (a polynomial upper bound alone does not rule out geometric convergence); quadratically if $e_{k+1}\le Ce_k^2$ with $C\gt0$ (scalar Newton's method near a regular root of a $C^2$ function, from a sufficiently close initial point).

entire_candidate_literal.source_text:
Fact — Formulas for the common induced norms
    
      For $m,n\ge1$, $\|A\|_1=\max_j\sum_i|a_{ij}|$ (largest absolute column sum); $\|A\|_\infty=\max_i\sum_j|a_{ij}|$ (largest absolute row sum); $\|A\|_2=\sigma_{\max}(A)=\sqrt{\lambda_{\max}(A^\top A)}$, the spectral norm (Section 5); mixed: $\|A\|_{p\to\infty}=\max_i\|a_{i,:}\|_q$ with $\tfrac1p+\tfrac1q=1$ (e.g. $\|A\|_{2\to\infty}$ is the largest row length, $\|A\|_{1\to\infty}=\max_{ij}|a_{ij}|$) and $\|A\|_{1\to p}=\max_j\|a_{:,j}\|_p$.

entire_candidate_literal.source_text: Proofs. $|(Ax)_i|\le\sum_j|a_{ij}|\,\|x\|_\infty$, attained by $x_j=\mathrm{sign}(a_{i^\star j})$ for the worst row $i^\star$. $\|Ax\|_1\le\sum_j|x_j|\sum_i|a_{ij}|$, attained at $x=e_{j^\star}$. Each output coordinate $a_{i,:}x$ is bounded by $\|a_{i,:}\|_q\|x\|_p$ (Hölder, attainable). $\square$ Running example $A=\begin{bmatrix}2 & 2\\ -1 & 1\end{bmatrix}$: $\|A\|_1=3$, $\|A\|_\infty=4$ (at $x=(1,1)$), $\|A\|_{1\to\infty}=2$, $\|A\|_{2\to\infty}=\sqrt8$, $\|A\|_2=2\sqrt2\approx2.83$: the longest semi-axis of the ellipse $A$ makes of the unit circle (Section 5, explorer).

entire_candidate_literal.source_text: The image of a box is a zonotope. For $\varepsilon>0$, $W$ maps $\{\|\delta\|_\infty\le\varepsilon\}$ to a sum of segments $\varepsilon[-w_j,w_j]$ over its columns (a parallelogram for invertible $2\times2$ $W$). The tightest enclosing box has half-widths $\varepsilon\|w_{i,:}\|_1$, which is what interval bound propagation keeps: for $W=\begin{bmatrix}1 & 1\\ 1 & -1\end{bmatrix}$, $\varepsilon=1$, the image is the square with corners $(\pm2,0),(0,\pm2)$, area $8$, inside the box $[-2,2]^2$ of area $16$.

current_missing_requirements: The norm-ball/image/scaled-segment correspondence needs epsilon>=0; the printed nondegenerate invertible parallelogram needs epsilon>0. The exact one-phrase positive-radius proposal supplies both.

entire_candidate_literal.source_text: Covering numbers. Assume $s\ge0$, $\tau>0$ and $d\ge1$. A cube of side $s$ lies in the $\ell_2$ ball of radius $s\sqrt d/2$ about its centre. Cutting $[0,1]^d$ into $m^d$ cubes with $m=\lceil\sqrt d/(2\tau)\rceil$ covers it by $m^d$ balls of radius $\tau$; their centres form a $\tau$-net, and the fewest balls that suffice is the covering number $M(\tau,[0,1]^d)$. For $\tau=0.1$: $64$ balls in $d=2$, about $1.1\times10^{12}$ in $d=10$. If an $L$-Lipschitz function has margin $m_0$ at every net point, its margin is at least $m_0-L\tau$ everywhere (Primer B).

current_missing_requirements: The printed side/reciprocal cutting formulas need s>=0,tau>0,d>=1. The exact proposed opening supplies these domains; no zero-radius finite cover or ordinary zero-dimension cutting is inferred.

entire_candidate_literal.source_text: Signed distance and Hausdorff distance. For a closed set $C$ with $C\ne\emptyset$ and $C^c\ne\emptyset$, a signed distance equals $\mathrm{dist}(x,C)$ on one side of the boundary and $-\mathrm{dist}(x,\text{complement})$ on the other; which side is positive is a declared convention (reachability modules put the safe side positive). It vanishes on the boundary, so "$\ell\gt0$" and "$\ell\ge0$" differ exactly there. The Hausdorff distance $d_H(A,B)=\max\{\sup_{a\in A}\mathrm{dist}(a,B),\sup_{b\in B}\mathrm{dist}(b,A)\}$ compares nonempty compact sets, e.g. $d_H([0,1],[0,2])=1$.

current_missing_requirements: The finite real signed-distance construction requires nonempty closed C and nonempty complement for zero iff boundary; current205 omits these proper/nonempty qualifications. Full-space real-distance totalization countermodel is explicit.

entire_candidate_literal.source_text: For $e_0,\varepsilon\gt0$, the geometric envelope $q^ke_0$ is at most $\varepsilon$ iff $k\ge\ln(e_0/\varepsilon)/\ln(1/q)$; this cutoff suffices for any errors $e_k\le q^ke_0$, and grows like $\ln(1/\varepsilon)$ as $\varepsilon\downarrow0$ with fixed $q\in(0,1)$ and $e_0$. For the exact errors $e_k=1/\sqrt k$, $k\ge1$, reaching the tolerance is equivalent to $k\ge1/\varepsilon^2$. At $\varepsilon=10^{-6}$ and $e_0=1$, the two exact envelopes first reach the tolerance at $20$ iterations for $q=0.5$ and at $10^{12}$, respectively; faster errors can reach it earlier. On a logarithmic plot exact positive geometric errors form a straight line, while the logarithmic slope of a positive reciprocal-power curve tends to zero (see the explorer). Used for geometric Lyapunov decay and interior-point iteration counts $O(\sqrt n\log(1/\varepsilon))$ in Module 2, $O(1/\sqrt T)$ primal-dual rates in Module 8, and gradient descent in Primer B.
